newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Nov 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Nov 11.

text.p: Drug wholesaler Bergen Brunswig Corp has signed a merger deal with generic drug maker Ivax in a $1.65 billion stock swap, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.
- Toyota Motor Corp will introduce a car with an engine that is one-third cheaper to make.
- Loral Space and Communications Ltd is close to signing an agreement with China to distribute phone service for the company's Globalstar network.
- Texaco Inc is trying to settle a race discrimination suit in which employees are seeking $71 million in back pay.
- General Motors Corp said a tentative three-year labor contract will prevent it from improving efficiency in the near future.
- Volkswagen AG official Jose Ignacio Lopez will likely stand trial for industrial espionnage in Germany at the beginning of next year.
- IBM Corp has formed a division to popularize its network computers.
- China imposed a temporary ban on some U.S. textile, agricultural and alcohol imports.
- A team led by Lockheed Martin Corp won a $1.8 billion Pentagon contract for a missile-warning system.
- PCS phone ventures are starting to appear in several market.

- A small group of U.S. economists foresee the third quarter's slowdown to reverse itself as consumers start spending - The Securities and Exchange Commission is to set tougher rules listing standards for companies that trade on the Nasdaq SmallCap Market.
- U.S. liquor industry are planning their next move after lifting a voluntary ban on radio and television advertizing.

- Tax-exempt municipal bonds might not be as tax free as some investors believe. Milllions of dollars in the market could become taxable when investors stumble upon a twist in the federal tax code known as the alternative minimum tax.
- In an effort to ward off a hostile bid by a competitor, CSX Corp is trying to buy Conrail Inc using controversial tactics that have upset Conrail shareholders.
